item.title: Galxe sets shutdown timeline, with all campaigns ending Dec 5 – Link Galxe publi
item.description:
Galxe sets shutdown timeline, with all campaigns ending Dec 5 – Link

Galxe published a partner transition guide for winding down its quest and credential platform. New campaign creation stopped Nov 9, existing campaigns end by Dec 5 and reward claims close Dec 15. Projects can request refunds of Space deposits and unused Business+ fees until Dec 5, and unclaimed token rewards until Jan 15, 2027. Completed Earndrops let projects withdraw unclaimed tokens directly from the contract.

One of Web3's biggest quest platforms closing signals that the incentive-farming growth model is losing steam as projects look for real, retained users.

item.title: Swedish Bitcoin treasury firm H100 lost ~30 BTC trading part of its stack – Link
item.description:
Swedish Bitcoin treasury firm H100 lost ~30 BTC trading part of its stack – Link

Stockholm-listed H100 Group reported a loss of about 30 BTC, roughly $1.8M, in Q3 from its "active BTC pool," which it uses for trading, investment and collateral. The pool ended September with ~233 BTC, alongside 3,243 BTC in the long-term treasury. The active strategy, which includes derivatives, came with August's acquisition of Norway's NSD AS, a deal that also added ~2,455 BTC. The loss was under 1% of total holdings.

Treasury firms that trade their reserves to chase extra yield also take on trading risk, and that blurs the simple "buy and hold Bitcoin" pitch to shareholders.

item.title: Flop Network testnet goes live Nov 24, with airdrops tied to agent activity – Li
item.description:
Flop Network testnet goes live Nov 24, with airdrops tied to agent activity – Link

Flop Labs, whose post Arthur Hayes retweeted, will launch the Flop Network testnet on Nov 24 at 07:00 UTC. AI agents can join without approval or waitlists and claim testnet FLOP daily via Technocore chat or API for inference. Airdrops will be based on actual agent activity, so holding unused faucet tokens earns nothing. Miners and validators don't need to hold FLOP. Devnet data won't carry over. Validator slots open in daily batches, and mainnet rankings start only after a 14-day grace period.

Rewarding real usage instead of passive holding is a direct attempt to filter out airdrop farmers and test genuine demand for agent inference.

item.title: CryptoQuant: short-term holders are capitulating at an average 15% loss – Link C
item.description:
CryptoQuant: short-term holders are capitulating at an average 15% loss – Link

CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost said short-term holder SOPR has dropped below 0.993, a level that has historically marked mid- to long-term entry zones for Bitcoin. Short-term holders are realizing an average loss of about 15%, and more underwater BTC is flowing to exchanges, which points to actual selling rather than wallet shuffling. Darkfost noted the signal works best in bull markets and does not give exit points.

Short-term holder capitulation has often come before local bottoms, but in a bear market these losses can last longer than expected.

item.description:
Gold drops nearly 3% while Bitcoin is down 28% for the quarter – Link

Gold fell to $3,514 per ounce, its lowest since early September 2025, and is down 15% for the quarter. Bitcoin hovered near $61,900, a 28% quarterly decline. ING data shows the US two-year real yield above 2.40%, the highest since 2023, while 10- and 30-year real yields are at 20-year highs and the dollar index sits around 103.80.

Rising real yields and a strong dollar are pressuring every non-yielding asset at once. Bitcoin is trading as a macro asset, not a hedge.

item.title: Wrapped Monero token XMR1 crashes 99% after issuer-linked wallet sells $13.5M –
item.description:
Wrapped Monero token XMR1 crashes 99% after issuer-linked wallet sells $13.5M – Link

XMR1, a wrapped Monero token issued by swap service Wagyu and traded on Hyperliquid’s order book, fell from about $488 to $1 in roughly 30 minutes. A wallet funded by the token’s creator address had received 5.2M XMR1 and sold about $13.5M worth. It is still unclear whether the transfers were authorized or the result of compromised credentials. Native Monero and Hyperliquid’s XMR perps were unaffected and kept trading near $482.

Wrapped assets carry the issuer’s risk. When redemption depends on a single bridge operator, one compromised key can wipe out the peg in minutes.

item.title: North Korean hackers routed funds through Sky’s PSM, putting a $2.7B reserve at
item.description:
North Korean hackers routed funds through Sky’s PSM, putting a $2.7B reserve at freeze risk – Link

Inca Digital traced $518M in transactions from illicit-linked wallets through Sky’s Peg Stability Module, including $101.9M tied to North Korea and $91.5M connected to the Bybit hack. The PSM holds about $2.7B in USDC in a single wallet, so if Circle blacklists that address, all of it would be frozen together. Sky said the flagged activity is under 0.06% of total PSM volume and none of it came through its screened front-ends.

Sky now sits between permissionless DeFi and regulated finance. As its institutional ties grow, open access to the PSM is becoming a compliance liability.

item.description:
Sherwood Protocol winds down as growth falls short – Link

Sherwood Protocol, a Robinhood-ecosystem agent capital layer, announced it will gradually cease operations. The team said growth missed expectations and running its Guardian Network at the current scale had become unsustainable. The code will stay open source but will no longer be maintained.

A wind-down like this is a reminder that the economics of agentic infrastructure still have to work before the narrative can carry a protocol.

item.description:

San Francisco’s luxury market is already heating up: more than 210 homes have sold this year for at least $1M above asking, and Bezel’s local watch sales have doubled year-on-year.

A wave of AI-sector liquidity could spill into risk assets, and some of that newly unlocked capital may find its way into crypto.

item.title: Starknet proposal would hand stakers’ voting power to validators by default – Li
item.description:
Starknet proposal would hand stakers’ voting power to validators by default – Link

SNIP-45 would let validators vote with their delegators’ staked STRK by default, and holders could opt out or redirect their vote in a single transaction. The draft says only about 0.5% of staked STRK took part in recent votes, while delegators hold 91% of the staked supply. The governance vote runs Nov 27 – Dec 4.

The proposal could fix chronically low turnout, but it risks concentrating governance power in large operators such as exchanges and liquid-staking providers.

item.title: Ant International launches protocol for real-time settlement of tokenized deposi
item.description:
Ant International launches protocol for real-time settlement of tokenized deposits and MMFs – Link

Ant International launched the Whale Orchestration Protocol under the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s BLOOM initiative. It enables delivery-versus-payment settlement between tokenized deposits and tokenized money market funds. The protocol runs on WhaleRTP, Ant’s blockchain-based wholesale settlement platform, and pilot transactions have already been completed with DBS and Franklin Templeton.

Instant settlement between tokenized cash and yield-bearing funds is a key piece for on-chain corporate treasury and could speed up institutional RWA adoption in Asia.

item.title: Ledger expands hardware tampering probe to Germany and UAE – Link Ledger widened
item.description:
Ledger expands hardware tampering probe to Germany and UAE – Link

Ledger widened its investigation into a physical supply-chain tampering campaign after finding suspicious devices in Berlin and receiving loss reports in Dubai. The company said the new cases are part of the same incident first seen in Southeast Asia, where devices were modified to capture the recovery phrase during setup. Ledger said its secure chip and OS are not affected and no confirmed case involves a device bought on ledger.com.

Ledger’s own hardware isn’t the problem here. The risk is in third-party resale channels, which makes buying directly from the manufacturer a basic security step.

item.description:

Zcash's NU7 network upgrade reportedly made private transaction confirmations roughly three times faster. The community also opened a governance poll on cutting block times to 20 seconds and reallocating 50,000 ZEC in funding. ZEC rose about 3% to around $950–960.

Faster, cheaper private payments strengthen Zcash's core privacy-coin value proposition.

item.title: Solana ecosystem highlights real-world infrastructure stress tests at Breakpoint
item.description:
Solana ecosystem highlights real-world infrastructure stress tests at Breakpoint London – Link

Solana Foundation chair Lily Liu said the TRUMP coin launch and the October 2025 $20B liquidation event showed network resilience at 60,000 TPS with no downtime. DTCC also plans a tokenized securities pilot on Solana in H2 2027, and Schroders is deploying its first tokenized fund on the network this month.

The update points to continued institutional build-out on Solana and could support longer-term network usage and TVL.

item.title: Hackers compromise 178 major websites via Optimizely flaw to swap crypto wallet
item.description:
Hackers compromise 178 major websites via Optimizely flaw to swap crypto wallet addresses – Link

A vulnerability in Optimizely let attackers inject code that silently swapped users' crypto wallet addresses during transactions on 178 affected sites, including HSBC, BBC, and Ledger. Total funds stolen remain unknown.

The incident highlights a supply-chain attack vector that can affect even large trusted institutions and may force re-audits of third-party web tooling.

item.title: Lighter DEX suspends withdrawals after $10.4–15.5M exploit tied to leaked API ke
item.description:
Lighter DEX suspends withdrawals after $10.4–15.5M exploit tied to leaked API key – Link

Perpetual DEX Lighter halted all withdrawals and wallet creation after attackers compromised a market maker's API key and drained an estimated $10.4–15.5 million. Lighter said its smart contracts were unaffected, and stolen funds were traced moving through Hyperliquid and into Monero (XMR).

The incident highlights operational and API-key risk and could pressure confidence in perp DEXs using external market-maker integrations.

Backpack received Designated Contract Market and Derivatives Clearing Organization designations from the CFTC, allowing it to launch a US-regulated blockchain-based perpetual derivatives and clearing platform. Backpack's associated token briefly spiked ≈44% before pulling back.

The approval creates a compliant US pathway for on-chain derivatives and may support broader institutional adoption.
